questions.q: Why does an ad hoc approach like naming files model_v2_final_FINAL.pkl break down as a team scales?
options: Because filenames cannot contain version numbers
Because the parameters, metrics, and code version that matter have no structured place to live
Because Python cannot open files with underscores in the name
Because models trained by different people must use different file formats
questions.explain: The filename tells you nothing about which hyperparameters, data, or metrics produced it — the information that matters has no structured, queryable home.

questions.q: In MLflow, why is log_metric typically called with a step argument across a training loop?
options: To overwrite the previous metric value each time
Because metrics can only be logged once per run
So the metric becomes a time series you can plot as a curve, not a single overwritten value
Because step is required to close the run
questions.explain: Passing step on each call builds a time-stepped series (e.g. validation AUC per epoch) rather than leaving only the final value.

questions.q: Why does MLflow's Tracking Server separate a backend store from an artifact store?
options: Because MLflow cannot write both metadata and files to the same disk
Metadata needs to be queryable (a database); bulk files don't, and benefit from independent scaling as object storage
The backend store is only used in local development and never in production
Artifacts must always be stored on the same machine running the training job
questions.explain: The backend store (a database) answers queries like 'best run by accuracy'; the artifact store (typically object storage) holds large files and scales independently of that metadata query path.

options: It deploys the trained model automatically to production
It hooks the framework's own training call to capture the params and metrics it already knows about
It replaces the need for a tracking server entirely
It automatically tunes hyperparameters during training
questions.explain: Autologging integrates with a specific framework's training call (e.g. .fit()) to log what that framework already exposes, without the engineer writing explicit log_param/log_metric calls.

questions.q: In Weights & Biases, which call plays a role roughly equivalent to MLflow's start_run plus log_param combined?
options: wandb.log()
wandb.log_artifact()
wandb.init()
wandb.finish()
questions.explain: wandb.init() starts the run and accepts a config dict that serves the same purpose as MLflow's log_param calls.
